name: Evil-WinRM - Pass the Hash
description: Opens an interactive WinRM (PowerShell) session authenticating with an NT hash via -H. Requires the account to be in Remote Management Users and WinRM (5985/5986) reachable.

examples.label: WinRM shell with the NT hash

notes:
`evil-winrm -i <ip> -u user -H <nthash>` gets an interactive WinRM shell using the hash - clean, native, and the go-to once you have a local-admin NT hash and 5985 is open.
Also covered in: OSCP PEN-200 Chapter 19 (Password Attacks)

recommended.note: Hunt further creds on the box.

defense.why_it_works: evil-winrm authenticates over WinRM using an NTLM hash (-H) for an interactive PowerShell session on the target.
defense.prerequisites: A valid NTLM hash for a WinRM-enabled account and 5985/5986 reachable.
defense.impact: An interactive remote PowerShell session as the target account via PtH.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1550.002] Event 4624 Logon Type 3 with Authentication Package NTLM and LogonProcessName NtLmSsp, with NO preceding interactive logon for that account; the same NTLM hash authenticating from an unusual source; 4672 for privileged PtH.
defense.artifacts: An NTLM network logon (4624 type 3) from evil-winrm -H; a session as the target user without their plaintext password.
defense.prevention: Enable Credential Guard and disable NTLM where possible; [MITRE T1550.002 M1026 Privileged Account Management] never reuse local-admin passwords (LAPS) so one hash doesn't unlock the network; restrict lateral admin logons; monitor NTLM auth.
defense.evasion: PtH uses valid material so no password failures occur - it blends with normal NTLM auth; using an allowed source host and common hours reduces suspicion.
defense.misconfiguration: WMI (Windows Management Instrumentation) is enabled and accessible remotely (TCP 135 + dynamic RPC ports) with no namespace-level ACLs. Domain admin or local admin credentials are usable to execute methods on DCOM objects. WMI event subscriptions can be used for persistence. The same issue applies to WinRM (TCP 5985/5986) — if enabled, any account in the local administrators or Remote Management Users group can connect.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# WMI namespace with broad remote access:
# Default WMI namespace security — 'Remote Enable' granted to local admins
# Any account with local admin can:
Invoke-WmiMethod -Class Win32_Process -Name Create -ArgumentList 'calc.exe' -ComputerName target

# WinRM enabled (common on servers):
# winrm quickconfig (enables WinRM on all interfaces)
# Any local admin can: Enter-PSSession -ComputerName target -Credential admin
defense.secure_config:
# Restrict WMI remote access (namespace ACL):
# WMI Control (wmimgmt.msc) -> Root\CIMV2 -> Security:
# Remove 'Remote Enable' from non-admin groups
# Only grant specific service accounts the 'Execute Methods' right

# Restrict WinRM to specific hosts/subnets:
# New-Item -Path WSMan:\localhost\Listener\* -Transport HTTP -Force
# Set-Item -Path WSMan:\localhost\Listener\*\Address -Value 10.10.1.0/24

# Disable WinRM on workstations (leave enabled only on servers that need it):
Disable-PSRemoting -Force

# Monitor WMI persistence:
# Event 5861 (WMI event subscription created)
# Event 4688 (Process creation via WMI) — look for wmiprvse.exe as parent

# Firewall — block WMI ports from non-admin subnets:
# New-NetFirewallRule -Name 'Block WMI Remote' -Direction Inbound -Protocol TCP -LocalPort 135 -Action Block
